sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 / WebGPURenderer (WebGPU, automatic WebGL 2 fallback); Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; PeerJS 1.5.5; AI Hub session client 1.4.0; bundled with Bun
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural 3D cel shading, ink silhouettes, hand-hatched wallpaper and wood textures, muted teal and warm parchment
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer with authored AnimationClips: idle, walking, match striking, pickup nods, scare reactions, bat wings, spider legs, ghost floating, and opening doors; procedural flame and ward motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written minor-key waltz, synthesized footsteps, wind, matches, doors, stairs and creatures, plus pitched gibberish syllables; no audio files; music defaults to 10 percent
sourceInformation.online: 1–4 player ghost races through AI Hub Protocol v1; standalone four-digit room codes with BroadcastChannel locally and public PeerJS signaling / WebRTC between devices
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium / Playwright; real Rapier scripted escape without cheats; all 24 rooms; simulated standard gamepad and touch; offline audio RMS and peak analysis; two-page BroadcastChannel and actual WebRTC races; official AI Hub normal, adverse-network and host-leave checks. WebGL 2 is the visual stand-in for unreliable headless WebGPU presentation. Physical controller, TV, iOS Safari and cross-network NAT behavior: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Atari publisher page and original Atari instruction manual: 24 rooms, four floors, matchlight, single carried object, urn assembly, master key, scepter, bats, tarantulas, wall-passing ghost, nine lives, sound clues and difficulty variations. AI Hub protocol and primary engine documentation were also read.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu 26.04 on WSL2

testingFeedback: 14 issues found during testing and review: seven game or UX issues and seven test-environment or harness issues. The game issues were fixed; software-GPU presentation uses a documented visual stand-in.
0 gameplay-breaking issues. Three blockers affected testing: the headless GPU compositor setup, Chromium socket path length, and a stalled WebGPU readback call.

The complete escape through real Rapier movement and collisions, including key and scepter swaps, permanent unlocks, all three urn fragments, enemy damage, stairs and the final return. The official AI Hub harness was especially useful for lifecycle and networking.
Raw headless WebGPU screenshots and readback: they exposed software-adapter limitations and added little evidence about gameplay. State checks and WebGL 2 visual review were more useful.
engineFeedback: Procedural geometry, cel materials and native animation clips made it possible to give every room a consistent illustrated identity without external art files.

Yes. Headless WebGPU presentation and readback were unreliable, and short timed input holds were unreliable under software rendering. Tests now process input explicitly and freeze drawing during logic and protocol checks.
The room graph, one-hand inventory and permanent locks, enemy state machines and following ghost, controller menus, synthesized audio, attract director, and race lifecycle.
Keeping physics, native character clips, room changes, generated materials and a WebGPU renderer coordinated inside one self-contained document.
Provide a reliable, documented headless WebGPU validation and readback path for software adapters, including clear diagnostics when presentation is unavailable.
promptFeedback: The source, controller-first interface, procedural sound and complete-demo requirements gave the game a clear identity.
Standalone multiplayer was less specific than the AI Hub protocol. It was implemented as room-code ghost races using WebRTC across devices and BroadcastChannel in one browser.
Preserving the original one-object puzzle while making four floors, matchlight, danger and return trips readable in a modern 3D game.
Specify standalone hosting or transport expectations, and distinguish required browser support from the available software-rendered test stand-ins.

aiHub.name: The Fright House
aiHub.tagline: Some houses have good bones. This one keeps them.
aiHub.description: Explore a hand-inked mansion by matchlight, outwit bats and restless residents, and reunite a shattered urn. One free hand makes every key, scepter and urn piece a decision; race up to three ghostly rivals.
aiHub.controls: Left stick / WASD: move; Cross / E: interact; Square / Space: match; Circle / Q: drop; Triangle / Tab: map; R2 / Shift: hurry; Options / Esc: pause. Mouse: click to walk or interact, right-click match. Touch: drag to walk, tap match; assisted interactions.
